gates.claim: the two Vieta products hold on the arc: prod(1-x*y_j) = x and prod(1-y_j/x) = 1/x -- both already Lean-proved, both nonvanishing on |x|=1
Sum_j log(1 - x*y_j) is CONTINUOUS through the branch point and equals the continuous log of the symmetric product, branch integer 0
Sum_j log(1 - y_j/x) likewise equals -log x, continuously through the branch point
the reason: AT the collision the two colliding roots are equal, so the two log-terms being permuted are IDENTICAL -- a sum cannot notice a relabelling of equal terms
gates.note: this is a SQUARE-ROOT branch point, so separation ~ sqrt|delta phi|; even with phi_0 at working precision the residual separation is ~1e-19, not ~1e-38. That is the expected behaviour, not a failure to resolve the collision.

gates.claim: with both sums pinned, Sum_j dV/dx = -2 log(x)/x, and integrating along x = e^{i phi} gives S - S(1) = phi^2 -- checked directly on the arc

verdict.outcome: The transport argument is REPAIRED. Working with the two symmetric Vieta products instead of a per-root branch labelling, the sum of logs is continuous through the branch point and equals the continuous log of the product with branch integer 0.
verdict.why_it_works: at the collision the two colliding roots are EQUAL, so the two log-terms being permuted are identical. A sum cannot notice a relabelling of equal terms. The old argument tracked a labelling, which is precisely what a collision destroys.
verdict.already_in_lean: both products -- prod_one_sub_x_mul and prod_x_sub in QOU/QBeta/FiveTwoCyclotomicBloch.lean, sorry-free since #4658.
verdict.still_missing: the envelope theorem needs dy_j/dx, which does not exist AT the branch point. The fix is removability: S is analytic on the arc minus one point (the IFT applies there, discriminant non-zero) and continuous at it (Route 17), so the identity extends by Riemann's removable singularity theorem. Ordinary analysis, NOT written.
